newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 2.00 to 4.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 2.00 to 4.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 to 4.00 cents per lb lower on Thursday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.
"It's due lower on paper based on London," said one trader. "London's down $20, but was due higher."

London robusta futures defied $10 higher pre-opening expectations and headed lower early Thursday, pressured by trade selling. At the midday break, September was down $20, to $1,625, but well off the low of $1,603. November fell $41, to $1,609.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures ended lower, as speculators took profits following two consecutive sessions of sharp gains. September fell 2.55 cents, to 200.55, after ranging from 206.90 to 193.75. December sunk 4.45 cents, to 170.25 cents, while the rest closed down 3.95 to 4.20 cents.
The September/December switch widened to 30.30 cents compared with 28.40 cents at the close on Tuesday.
Technically, September support was pegged at 195.25-194.10 cents, followed by 192.00-191.20 cents, traders said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday that no damaging cold weather is expected into next week in Brazil's coffee belt. Cool, dry conditions are forecast for Sunday through Wednesday of next week, with low temperatures in the mid-40s to mid-50s F (7-13 C).
After Wednesday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 938 60-kg bags as of August 5, to 92,459 bags. An additional 6,447 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
